Nun
nŭn
n. (the Ephraimite father of Joshua — a patronymic so constant that the successor of Moses is scarcely ever named without it)
From Hebrew Nun, probably from a root meaning to propagate, to continue, or to flourish — the same word is the name of the fourteenth Hebrew letter. He is of the tribe of Ephraim, grandson of Elishama the prince (1Ch 7:26-27).

Biblical Definition

Nun is the father of Joshua, and Scripture will hardly let the son be mentioned without him: “Joshua the son of Nun” occurs some thirty times, from the wilderness to the book of Judges. He first appears when the young man will not leave the tent: “his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle” (Exo 33:11). He is one of the twelve spies, and it is at the sending that Moses changes his name: “Moses called Oshea the son of Nun Jehoshua” (Num 13:16) — from “salvation” to “the LORD is salvation”, the Hebrew name of which Jesus is the Greek. He and Caleb alone of that generation crossed Jordan. Moses laid hands on him: “Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him” (Deu 34:9), and the next book opens on the succession — “the LORD spake unto Joshua the son of Nun, Moses' minister” (Jos 1:1). Of Nun himself nothing is recorded. He is an Ephraimite who died in Egypt or in the wilderness, and whose name is written into the title of the man who took Israel into the land.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Nun as a person; in sacred history he is the father of Joshua, of the tribe of Ephraim, and the name is also that of a letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

expand to see more

NUN, n. The father of Joshua, of the tribe of Ephraim, descended from Elishama the prince of that tribe.

The name is thought to signify continuance or perpetuity.

Nun is also the name of the fourteenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

The son of Nun was called Oshea, and Moses named him Jehoshua.

He was Moses' minister, and succeeded him in the leading of Israel into Canaan.

Key Scripture

Exo 33:11 — "And the LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend. And he turned again into the camp: but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle."

Num 13:16 — "These are the names of the men which Moses sent to spy out the land. And Moses called Oshea the son of Nun Jehoshua."

Deu 34:9 — "And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the LORD commanded Moses."

Jos 1:1 — "Now after the death of Moses the servant of the LORD it came to pass, that the LORD spake unto Joshua the son of Nun, Moses' minister, saying,"

Modern Corruption

Succession in the church is treated as an institutional mechanism; Joshua was prepared for it by years of attending on Moses in the tabernacle before any hands were laid on him.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is how the Bible produces a successor. Long before Deu 34:9 and the laying on of hands, there is Exo 33:11: a young man who “departed not out of the tabernacle” when the great man had gone back to the camp. Joshua was formed by proximity to the presence of God and by years of ordinary attendance on Moses — carrying, waiting, going up the mountain part of the way, standing at the door. Then came the commission, and the office was laid on a man already shaped for it. The New Testament pattern is identical: Timothy attended Paul, was proved, and only then received the laying on of the hands of the presbytery, and the rule stands — “Lay hands suddenly on no man” (1Ti 5:22).

The renaming in Num 13:16 is worth a second look. Oshea means salvation; Moses prefixes the covenant name and makes it “the LORD is salvation”. The point is not decorative. Twelve men were about to go into the land and ten of them would come back reckoning by their own strength, and the leader of the two who did not was sent out with a name that answered the question of the whole expedition. The Greek of that name is Iesous, Jesus, and Hebrews notes the type: the Joshua who gave them rest in Canaan did not give the true rest, so “there remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God” (Heb 4:9).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Nun (H5126), Nun; Hoshea' (H1954), Oshea, salvation; Yehoshua' (H3091), Joshua, the LORD is salvation; Greek Iesous (G2424).

expand to see more

Hebrew Nun (H5126) — Nun; an Ephraimite, father of Joshua, of the house of Elishama.

Hebrew Hoshea' (H1954) — Oshea, Hosea; salvation, deliverance — Joshua's original name.

Hebrew Yehoshua' (H3091) — Jehoshua, Joshua; “the LORD is salvation”, the name Moses gave him.

Greek Iesous (G2424) — Jesus; the Greek of the same name, used of Joshua in Act 7:45 and Heb 4:8.

Hebrew mesharet (H8334) — a minister, attendant; Joshua's standing title before he was leader.

Usage

"“His servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man” — the apprenticeship at the tent door."

"“Moses called Oshea the son of Nun Jehoshua” — a name changed before a hard errand."

"“Joshua the son of Nun, Moses' minister” — how the book of the conquest opens."
